correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(\dot W=2\gamma(x^2+y^2)-8\alpha z\) and exact sign preservation of \(z\). For a compact ergodic invariant measure off the plane, applying Birkhoff recurrence to \(\log|z|\) yields \(\int xy\,d\mu=-\alpha\) without requiring global integrability of \(\log|z|\); invariance of the bounded smooth observable \(W\) then gives the mean-height identity. The plane law \(\dot q=2\gamma q\) excludes nontrivial compact invariant probabilities there when \(\gamma\ne0\). At \(\gamma=0\), polar reduction gives \(\dot\theta=1-r^2\cos^2\theta\), hence exactly the circles \(0<r<1\) with period \(2\pi/\sqrt{1-r^2}\). For \(\gamma<0,z\ge0\), \(W\ge0\) and \(\dot W\le-\min(2|\gamma|,2\alpha)W\), giving global exponential collapse. Independent symbolic checks reproduced the central identities.
residual_risks: The invariant-measure theorem is componentwise for compactly supported ergodic measures; it does not classify the negative-\(z\) half-space.
